warnings: Render/technical: Increase samples substantially and enable a strong denoiser (OIDN/OptiX). Also clamp indirect/specular to reduce fireflies while iterating.

Core effect workflow: If this is coming from volumes/particles, switch to a surface-based liquid representation (mesh the sim / particle-to-mesh) so the pour has a continuous refractive surface. Without a contiguous surface, it will not read as water/wine.

Material sanity check: ensure the liquid is not emissive. If emission is contributing, reduce it hard: Line 299 (emission Strength) → try 0.0–0.2 (or disable emission entirely for a realistic liquid).

Absorption tuning: Line 258 (Volume Absorption Density = 12.0) is likely making the fluid look overly thick/cloudy at this scene scale. Try 1.0–4.0 for wine (depends on thickness units), and near-0 for water (or very low with slight tint).
Reduce procedural micro-noise that’s reading as “grain”: Line 152 (noise Detail 8.0) → 2–4; Line 175 (bump Strength 0.25) → 0.03–0.08; Line 183 (mix Factor 0.35) → 0.10–0.20 to lessen noisy breakup.

Calm the wave distortion: Line 146 (wave Distortion 6.0) → 1.0–2.5; consider lowering Line 145 (wave Scale 18.0) if the surface looks like turbulent shader noise rather than physically driven ripples.

Lighting/readability: Provide a stronger environment reflection source for clean specular cues (even a dim HDRI or larger soft area light). If you keep the dark mood, increase background strength slightly: Line 101 (bg Strength 0.12) → 0.2–0.5 so the liquid has something to reflect.
Camera/DOF: Reduce DOF blur or move the focus plane onto the stream so at least part of the pour is tack-sharp; keep cinematic DOF only after the liquid reads correctly.
